newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares retreat 1.2 pct on foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares retreat 1.2 pct on foreign selling.

text.p: Selective buying by local mutual funds failed to offset sales by foreign investors and speculators which pushed Delhi shares to a lower close on Wednesday, brokers said.
The Delhi sensitive index ended down 9.65 points, or 1.2 percent, at 776.71.
"The sentiment was dampened as speculators started squaring up positions which they had built since the presentation of the budget on February 28," said Vinod Gupta of brokers Fairdeal Investments.
Share prices had rallied after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presented the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on February 28.
ACC closed one rupee down at 1,658.
State Bank of India lost 2.65 rupees at 302.35.
Larsen and Toubro ended 3.30 rupees lower at 237.50.
